A_target.statement:
Let $K / F$ be a [[Definition:Galois Extension|Galois extension]] and $E$ an intermediate field with $E / F$ [[Definition:Normal Extension|normal]].
Then:
:$\Gal {E / F} \cong \Gal {K / F} / \Gal {K / E}$

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|homomorphism]] with [[Definition:Kernel of Group Homomorphism|kernel]] $N$.
Then:
:$H \cong G / N$

substitutions.the surjective homomorphism: restriction of automorphisms of K to the intermediate field E
substitutions.the kernel of the map: the automorphisms of K fixing E pointwise
substitutions.the target of the map: the Galois group of E over F

derived.the target as a collapsed source: the Galois group of E over F as a quotient of that of K over F

validity_conditions: Restriction to E is well defined precisely because E is normal over F, so every automorphism of K maps E to itself.
Restriction is surjective onto the Galois group of E over F, since every automorphism of E extends to K by the isomorphism extension theorem.
Its kernel is the automorphisms fixing E pointwise, and normality of that subgroup corresponds exactly to normality of the intermediate extension.
proof_plan:
As $E / F$ is [[Definition:Normal Extension|normal]], every $F$-embedding of $E$ into $K$ maps $E$ into itself.
Hence $\sigma \restriction_E \in \Gal {E / F}$, and $\rho$ is a [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|homomorphism]].

Every $\tau \in \Gal {E / F}$ extends to an automorphism of $K$, since $K / F$ is [[Definition:Normal Extension|normal]].
Hence $\rho$ is [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]].

We have:
:$\map \ker \rho = \set {\sigma: \sigma \restriction_E = \operatorname {id}_E} = \Gal {K / E}$
By the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]]:
:$\Gal {E / F} \cong \Gal {K / F} / \Gal {K / E}$
{{qed}}
